correctness.rationale: Exact block algebra gives a triangular similarity with diagonal eigenvalues 1 and (T+WT^{-1}W)(T+alpha I)^{-1}. The stationary spectrum is {0} plus the real generalized eigenspectrum of (alpha I-B,T+alpha I). For every nonzero vector u, derivative of q_alpha(u) is strictly positive because T+B is SPD; compactness upgrades this to strict monotonicity of both spectral extrema for all eigenvalue multiplicities. Their summed signs cross exactly once, establishing the unique sharp minimizer. q_alpha(u)<1 and q_alpha(u)>-1 iff 2alpha>lambda_max(B-T), which proves the exact stability range and strict boundary. A trace equation gives the exact n=2 shift. The included independent-formula/checker code reproduces noncommuting and nilpotent examples and 80 additional finite cases; finite tests are ancillary to the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The fully read 2026 VBP primary work establishes block and spectral machinery but does not determine the sharp global unique stationary radius minimizer for all noncommuting SPD–indefinite pairs. Primary comparison with distinct 2018 relaxed splitting, later PMBP abstract, and published published-finding corpus searches did not reveal an equivalent or dominating VBP optimum. Classical equioscillation is credited; the novelty is the exact VBP application, strict all-dimensional balancing proof, stability frontier and coupling-independent two-dimensional formula. Residual full-text access and alias risks remain.
residual_risks: The full Xie–Huang–Cui–Li 2024 PMBP paper was not accessible; while its block family differs, it may conceal a more general optimality theorem under an alternative formulation.
An equivalent theorem may exist in classic generalized eigenvalue/iterative splitting literature under another name; searched records do not prove absence.
Zhang–Dai 2017 full text was not materially inspected; only abstract and source-side comparison support inapplicability.

value.rationale: For the actual 2026 VBP scheme the theorem uniquely and constructively optimizes asymptotic stationary convergence for arbitrary noncommuting indefinite W and SPD T, provides the exact stability threshold and an off-diagonal-insensitive 2x2 shift formula, and gives a practically meaningful warning that the published Frobenius distance choice can make its stationary error iterate divergent (rho about 15.999728) while alpha*=16 gives zero spectral radius. This answers a natural untuned parameter question in the source without asserting the claim for outer flexible GMRES.
